channel.title: Gabriel Paiva · Blog
channel.description: Backend, self-hosting and the projects behind them.

item.title: I turned a dusty school laptop into my server (and the network was the hard part)
item.description: A laptop bought for online school sat unused for four years. Now it runs my projects. This is how it got there, what broke along the way, and what's still missing.

item.title: Learning Go by building a family cloud: highlights from a 25-entry devlog
item.description: I came from Node and Express and wanted to learn Go and SvelteKit by shipping something real. The devlog tells the story: the wrong turns, the Go moments, and an honest verdict from the people who used it.

item.title: Legacy, part 1: how we won a one-day hackathon (and why it isn't over)
item.description: A pen-and-paper morning, a four-hour build and a frontend-only pitch won us first place at the TeamGreen4All hackathon. Here's how the day went and what I owned.

item.title: A day at Celfocus: what I took from the Insider open day
item.description: I spent a day at Celfocus's Porto office for their Insider open day: a talk, job shadowing and a lot of conversations. Here's the experience, kept general on purpose.

item.title: Porto Tech Hub 2025: what I did with one ticket
item.description: Tickets to Porto Tech Hub were limited and handed out by my school. Here's how I used mine: one talk about writing beautiful code, every company table, and the closing ceremony.

item.title: The prize was a book, so I spent the summer building something with it
item.description: PlanIt won a Vue book at ESMAD, so I spent my summer building a project next to it. Here's what that taught me, including what I got wrong about my own TypeScript.
